WIDER CONTEXT
- In August 2021 a letter to Geneva's mayor, Frédérique Perler, signed by about 100 people from the cultural sector, questioned the choice of Marc-Olivier Wahler as director. Named signatories included the historian Bernard Lescaze, the former Conseiller d'État Laurent Moutinot and Erica Deuber Ziegler (Radio Lac, 17 August 2021).
- The letter accused Wahler of not understanding the museum's collections, spending too much on communication and showing contempt for staff. The SIT union secretary Valérie Buchs confirmed the criticism; unions said management was too top-down and staff were never consulted, which they considered typical of all City institutions (Radio Lac).
- The petitioners denounced "historical nonsense liable to mislead the public who visit" and accused Wahler of planning to replace the graphics cabinet with a café (The Art Newspaper, 27 September 2021). Le Temps counted 117 signatures on the petition and quoted its complaints of "méconnaissance de l'essence même des collections" (lack of knowledge of the very essence of the collections; translated) (Le Temps, 19 November 2021).
- Wahler replied that he wanted to move the graphics cabinet to give it more space, called the overspending accusations false, citing several official audits of the accounts that found no grounds for complaint, and said the protesters wanted to keep the museum "the domain of an elite" (The Art Newspaper).
- Sami Kanaan, Geneva's top culture official, said he backed Wahler's vision and had "no hesitation about appointing him permanently from November" (The Art Newspaper, citing Le Temps). Wahler's two years in post ended on 1 November 2021 and he was confirmed in the job (Le Temps).

ID: mus-e-national-du-bardo-tunis

Red flags: 2021 to 2023 closure during the parliament shutdown
- President Kais Saied closed the museum when he shut parliament, which shares the same building; he sent tanks to surround parliament on 25 July 2021 in moves his critics called a coup (Reuters via Arab News, 5 September 2023).
- In April 2023 the museum had been closed for over 21 months with no official explanation; reopening dates of 20 March, 18 April and 2 May 2023 came and went, and unattributed statements said "tout est prêt depuis un moment, dans l'attente d'un feu vert de la présidence de la République" (everything has been ready for a while, waiting for a green light from the presidency; translated) (Webdo, Hatem Bourial, 17 April 2023).
- In August 2023 Kapitalis wrote that the museum stayed closed although parliament had reopened months earlier, and quoted Hassen Zargouni, head of Sigma Conseil: "La fermeture prolongée du Musée du Bardo n'est ni justifiable ni souhaitable pour nous autres Tunisiens" (the prolonged closure of the Bardo Museum is neither justifiable nor desirable for us Tunisians; translated). Zargouni rejected security, funding and renovation as explanations and asked whether it was a matter of political will (Kapitalis, Imed Bahri, 19 August 2023).
- The museum reopened on 14 September 2023 after more than two years; at the ceremony the culture minister Hayet Ketat Guermazi said it "avait continué de fonctionner" (had continued to operate; translated) (Webmanagercenter, 14 September 2023).

- https://www.arabnews.com/node/2368136/amp

Red flags: 2023 objections to the prolonged closure
- In April 2023 the museum had been closed for more than 21 months; planned reopenings around 20 March and on 18 April 2023 had not taken place, no official source had spoken, and the only statements said "tout est prêt depuis un moment, dans l'attente d'un feu vert de la présidence de la République" ("everything has been ready for a while, waiting for a green light from the presidency of the Republic", translated) (Webdo, Hatem Bourial, 17 April 2023).
- In August 2023 Kapitalis wrote that the museum stayed closed although the parliament sharing its site had reopened months earlier, and quoted Hassen Zargouni, head of Sigma Conseil: "La fermeture prolongée du Musée du Bardo n'est ni justifiable ni souhaitable pour nous autres Tunisiens" ("The prolonged closure of the Bardo Museum is neither justifiable nor desirable for us Tunisians", translated). Zargouni rejected security, money and works as explanations and asked whether it was a matter of the authorities' will (Kapitalis, Imed Bahri, 19 August 2023).
- In September 2023 Reuters reported that there had been no firm information about the reopening since the new parliament started work that year (Reuters via Arab News, 5 September 2023).
- At the reopening ceremony on 14 September 2023 the culture minister Hayet Ketat Guermazi said that "contrairement à ce qui a été dit, le musée avait continué de fonctionner" ("contrary to what was said, the museum had continued to operate", translated) and that staff had worked throughout to finish a careful restoration (Webmanagercenter, 14 September 2023).
